title: Patagonia 2026 Drone Panorama and Post-Processing Workflow

date.basis: embedded_creation_time in metadata (2026-04-17); video filename indicates Patagonia 2026 context

locations.name: Patagonia, Monte Fitz Roy region, Argentina
locations.basis: Transcript repeatedly references Patagonia and Fitz Roy; scene context and mountains align with Monte Fitz Roy region

summary: The video presents an on-location workflow for drone-based panorama work in Patagonia, focusing on planning wide and panoramic shots, evaluating light and composition, and executing a non-destructive, tiered post-processing workflow in RAW and Photoshop. It covers panorama stitching with PT GUI, projection decisions (rectilinear vs cylindrical), cropping choices (2x3, 4x5, wide-angle) to optimize leading lines, and a sequence of local and global adjustments (whites, color temperature, tint, color separation, selective color, color grading, and camera calibration). The narration also details using non-destructive techniques like the history brush, multiple adjustment layers, and targeted tools (dodge/burn, puppet warp, perspective warp, and blur vignette) to balance mountains, sky, and foreground while preserving atmosphere.

landscape-to-intimate scene range

sections.description: The narrator sets the scene by contrasting grand landscape stitches with small riverfront intimate frames, notes lighting variations, and introduces two quick processing cues: wider images and higher dynamic range tend to require more localized, blended adjustments.

sections.title: Rule of six and initial panorama evaluation

leading elements and focal points in each sixth
criteria for discarding panos without proper leading lines
sections.description: The speaker emphasizes a compositional rule—divide the frame into six equal sections and ensure each contains something contributing to the composition—before selecting a panorama that has a strong leading line and avoid empty sixths.

concepts: panorama vs single-shot evaluation
light distribution and scene depth
decision-making about which panorama to pursue based on light and composition
sections.description: Discussion centers on choosing between multiple panorama candidates, comparing wide-angle vs free-pano approaches, and prioritizing shots with favorable light distribution and leading-line continuity.

exposure, shadows, blacks, and clipping management
color temperature and tint tweaks

sections.description: The presenter demonstrates a quick, selective approach to RAW adjustments (whites replacement, temperature/tint shifts) and introduces the history brush as a non-destructive editing method, explaining how history can function like layers to restore or modify previous steps.

sections.description: A focused explanation of using selective color to selectively modify whites, blacks, and color channels, including a demonstration of color separation to enhance greens and reds, with cautions about artifact risk and natural saturation.

sections.title: Stitching workflows: PT GUI, projection choices, and composition tweaks

sections.description: This section walks through selecting files, aligning and stitching in PT GUI, adjusting projection to optimize perspective and distortion, and exploring wide-angle output with post-stitch cropping. It also covers workflow considerations when edge artifacts or extraneous drones intrude into the composition.

sections.title: Advanced multi-zone color grading, local adjustments, and final refinements

4-zone color grading, white/black balance, and blue handling

dodge & burn, depth layering, and atmosphere preservation
edge refinement, vignette strategies (blur vignette)
final checks: atmosphere and atmospheric priority in mid-day shoots
sections.description: The final portion delves into complex local adjustments across multiple zones (mountain, sky, foreground, foliage), including deep dives into color grading with highlights/shadows, calibration and selective color polish, and depth techniques like layer separation and controlled blur vignette. It culminates in dodge/burn planning, perspective concerns, and an emphasis on preserving atmospheric mid-day shots as a decisive factor in image quality.
